answer: Agents bond stake and prove membership in a Semaphore tree, then evaluate an epoch polynomial to produce rate-limit proofs tied to a nullifier. If an agent sends duplicate messages in the same epoch, the differing evaluations let observers use Shamir secret sharing to recover its private key, exposing the violation. The protocol can then slash bonded collateral immediately. This makes each permitted message a voyage across a narrow terrace, while the lotus-like nullifier marks the limit.
